subject: Follow-up: PulseLogic privacy & short-log option (post-discovery)
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@pulselogic.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Follow-up: PulseLogic privacy & short-log option (post-discovery)

Hi Oliver — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment:

Summary of ask:
- PulseLogic needs assurance that any PII in user inputs is not retained (0-retention)
- You’re open to Redwood keeping short debug logs (non-PII) for a limited window to support incidents / tuning
- Residency: core inference processing must be in EU region for this deal

What we can propose today (initial):
- PII: pipeline-level redaction + optional customer-side tokenization, 0-retention for identified PII
- Short logs: up to 72 hours for non-PII telemetry (request metadata + model performance traces) encrypted at rest
- SOC2 evidence and model access controls: we can share our SOC2 + technical runbook (link below)

Immediate next steps I’ll take:
1) Loop in Aditya (privacy engineering) to propose the exact redaction approach and controls.
2) Share a short write-up with the configuration options and sample contract language for the retention carveout.
3) If this looks good, we can set up a 30-minute technical pilot kickoff next week (canary with sample traffic).

Attachments: proposed-ephemeral-policy.pdf (short draft for PulseLogic)
Related links: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567

Thanks — will follow up with the technical note by EOD.

— Neha Kapoor
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@pulselogic.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: contracts@pulselogic.ai
Date: Wed, 03 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PulseLogic privacy & short-log option (post-discovery)

Hi Neha — thanks for the concise recap. That matches what we discussed. A couple of clarifying points from my side:

1) By PII we mean any user-entered free text that includes names, national identifiers, account numbers, or direct contact info. PulseLogic requires 0-retention for those inputs unless redacted before transmission to Redwood.
2) We’re comfortable with short, non-PII logs for 72 hours for debugging, but any logs that could materially reconstruct user inputs are not acceptable.
3) Residency: all inference must execute in EU region. Metadata can be sent to tooling outside EU if encrypted and if we add it to our DPA; final decision TBD by legal.

Legal asks: our GC requests:
- SOC2 Type II report (recent) and any relevant penetration test summaries
- A draft retention clause we can review and iterate on

Happy to run a pilot. If you can share the privacy draft and evidence we’ll route to Legal and Security. Can you also include a short note on how key management would work (KMS options)?

Oliver
Head of Product, PulseLogic
oliver.chen@pulselogic.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@pulselogic.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -0500
Subject: RE: Follow-up: PulseLogic privacy & short-log option (post-discovery)

Hi Oliver — looping in with a technical proposal and mitigations. High-level approach that meets the bullets above:

Technical proposal (summary):
- PII handling: two-layer approach: 1) Customer-side pre-ingest redaction library (recommended) that can run before sending any user text to Redwood; 2) Server-side redaction: pattern + ML classifier that strips or replaces detected PII tokens before storage.
- Storage policy: PII-marked content is never persisted to disk or long-term storage; it is processed in-memory only and excluded from KV cache writes.
- Short logs: we retain non-PII telemetry and model performance traces for 72 hours in an encrypted S3 bucket (EU region). Logs are encrypted with customer-managed KMS (option) or Redwood KMS (default).
- Auditability: we provide access logs and an exportable evidence package for the pilot (redaction logs show counts only, not original text).
- Canary/pilot: we can configure a canary that routes 0.5–2% of traffic through a monitored stack so you can validate redaction and debugability without broad exposure.

Limitations & tradeoffs:
- Zero technical guarantee against all semantic leakage without customer-side redaction. Server-side classifiers reduce risk but are probabilistic.
- Debugging fidelity will be reduced when PII is redacted; we can offer a debug-mode that temporarily increases retention for a short, auditable window if you authorize it via a documented process.

Attachments: privacy-evidence.zip (sample SOC2 abstracts, redaction classifier accuracy), proposed-ephemeral-policy.pdf (same as Neha’s)

Suggested contract language (snippet, for your GC):
"Redwood will not persist customer-identified PII received via API beyond transient in-memory processing. Non-PII telemetry will be retained for a maximum of 72 hours in encrypted storage located in the EU. Customer may opt for customer-managed KMS keys for all log encryption."

If that aligns, Neha — can you share a trimmed contract clause and a one-pager for the pilot scope? Oliver — we can turn around a pilot config and SOC materials this week.

— Aditya Rao
Privacy & Platform Security Lead | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

From: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@pulselogic.ai>

Cc: contracts@pulselogic.ai
Date: Thu, 04 Mar 2027 16:30:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Follow-up: PulseLogic privacy & short-log option (post-discovery)

Thanks Aditya/Neha — that level of detail helps. PulseLogic legal will review the suggested clause and SOC files. A couple quick confirmations before we route internally:

- We prefer customer-managed KMS for logs if possible — please include the steps for CMK setup in the pilot doc.
- We expect to see the redaction false-negative rate (classifier miss rate) in the evidence package — even rough numbers are helpful.
- If pilot looks good, procurement will request a 30–60 day evaluation with an SLA exception for EU-only processing for the pilot period.

Please send the pilot config + contract snippet and we’ll start the legal loop.

Oliver
Head of Product | PulseLogic
